## Q ai-20261022-a11-16
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: IAM, STS
- tags: federation, oidc, iam-roles, least-privilege
- difficulty: medium
- time: 120
- skills: 1.1.k2, 1.1.s3, 1.1.k4
- concept: An IAM OIDC identity provider lets an external CI platform assume a scoped role with temporary credentials instead of long-term keys
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Pipeline ngoài AWS cần bỏ khóa dài hạn và chỉ cho đúng repository/nhánh — cơ chế federation nào cấp credential tạm?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company's deployment pipeline runs on GitHub Actions, outside AWS. The pipeline currently deploys to an AWS account with an IAM user's access key stored as a repository secret. A security audit requires removing long-term credentials from the pipeline, and the deployment permissions must be usable only by workflows that run from one specific repository and its main branch. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

- A. Create an IAM OIDC identity provider for the GitHub token issuer and a role whose trust policy accepts tokens whose audience claim is sts.amazonaws.com
- B. Create an IAM Roles Anywhere trust anchor and issue an X.509 client certificate to each workflow runner, stored in the repository as an encrypted secret and renewed on a schedule
- C. Create an IAM OIDC identity provider for the GitHub token issuer and a role whose trust policy accepts tokens only when the subject claim matches the repository and branch
- D. Run self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Amazon EC2 for the repository and branch, and let the deployment workflows use the instance profile's temporary credentials

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** The OIDC provider lets the workflow exchange its signed token for temporary credentials, and a condition on the subject claim in the role's trust policy limits the role to one repository and branch, so no long-term key exists.
- Trust policy that checks the audience claim alone: any GitHub repository could assume the role (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Roles Anywhere with certificates per runner: needs certificate issuance and renewal plus a private key secret (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Self-hosted runners on EC2: removes keys, but adds runner instances to patch and scale (tốn vận hành hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_create_oidc.html
> 🇻🇳 CI bên ngoài AWS bỏ access key → IAM OIDC provider + role có điều kiện claim sub (repo/nhánh), không chỉ aud.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-17
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security

- difficulty: medium
- time: 140
- skills: 1.1.k5, 1.1.k4
- concept: Shared responsibility evidence: AWS Artifact for AWS-side attestations, AWS Config conformance packs for the customer's own configuration
- refs: A-nen-tang-kien-truc.md, B-bao-mat-compliance.md
- hint: Một bằng chứng thuộc "bảo mật của đám mây" (phía AWS), một bằng chứng thuộc "bảo mật trong đám mây" (phía bạn) — công cụ nào cho từng loại?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company is preparing for a PCI DSS assessment. The assessors ask for two kinds of evidence: independent attestations covering the physical data centers and the AWS-managed infrastructure, and continuous evidence that the company's own Amazon S3 buckets and security groups meet the required configuration standards. The company wants to produce this evidence with the LEAST operational overhead. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Enable AWS Security Hub with the PCI DSS standard and export its findings as the attestation for the physical data centers and the AWS-managed infrastructure
- B. Download the AWS PCI DSS attestation of compliance and the related audit reports from AWS Artifact on demand at no charge
- C. Create an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail and give the assessors the logged API calls as evidence of the S3 bucket and security group configuration
- D. Deploy an AWS Config conformance pack that evaluates the company's S3 buckets and security groups against the required configuration rules
- E. Run an AWS Config advanced query that exports the current S3 bucket and security group configurations, and give the assessors that snapshot

**Answer:** B, D

**Explanation:** AWS Artifact provides on-demand compliance reports for the infrastructure AWS secures, and a Config conformance pack continuously evaluates the customer's own resources, which are the customer's side of the shared responsibility model.
- Security Hub PCI DSS findings: evaluate the company's resources, not AWS data centers or AWS-managed infrastructure (đặt sai chỗ)
- CloudTrail API history: shows who changed what, not whether resources meet the standard (giải bài toán khác)
- One-time Config advanced query: a point-in-time snapshot, not continuous evidence (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/artifact/latest/ug/what-is-aws-artifact.html
> 🇻🇳 Bằng chứng phía AWS → AWS Artifact; bằng chứng cấu hình liên tục phía khách hàng → AWS Config conformance pack.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-18
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: IAM
- tags: least-privilege, access-analyzer, policy-generation
- difficulty: easy
- time: 105
- skills: 1.1.k4
- concept: IAM Access Analyzer generates a least-privilege policy from the CloudTrail activity of a role
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Role đã chạy hai tháng với quyền quản trị — công cụ nào dựng chính sách chỉ gồm các hành động thực sự được gọi, dựa trên log?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

An application's IAM role was created with the AdministratorAccess managed policy during development. The application has now run in production for two months, and AWS CloudTrail is logging management events for the account. The security team must replace the role's permissions with a policy that grants only the actions the application actually used. The team wants to do this with the LEAST manual effort. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate a policy from the role's CloudTrail activity, review it, and attach it in place of AdministratorAccess
- B. Use the IAM last accessed information to find the services the role used, and attach those services' AWS managed full-access policies in place of AdministratorAccess
- C. Query the role's CloudTrail events with Amazon Athena, list the distinct actions it called, and write a customer managed policy from the results
- D. Attach the AWS managed job function policy that best matches the application, such as PowerUserAccess, in place of AdministratorAccess

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** IAM Access Analyzer reviews the role's CloudTrail events over a chosen period and generates a policy with the actions actually used, which can be reviewed and attached instead of the broad managed policy.
- Full-access policies for the last-accessed services: grant every action of those services, not just the ones used (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Athena query and a hand-written policy: reaches the same result with more manual work (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Job function policy such as PowerUserAccess: still far broader than the actions used (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access-analyzer-policy-generation.html
> 🇻🇳 Thu hẹp quyền theo hành vi thực tế, ít công nhất → IAM Access Analyzer policy generation (dựa trên CloudTrail).

## Q ai-20261022-a11-19
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: IAM, IAM Identity Center
- tags: abac, tagging, iam-policies, least-privilege
- difficulty: hard
- time: 160
- skills: 1.1.s2
- concept: Attribute-based access control matches principal tags to resource tags so one policy scales to many projects
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Sáu mươi dự án, thêm mới mỗi tuần mà không viết policy mới — cần một điều kiện tự mở rộng theo dự án thay vì liệt kê từng tài nguyên.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company runs 60 projects in one AWS account. Each project team may start, stop and tag only the Amazon EC2 instances that belong to its own project. Engineers sign in through IAM Identity Center, and new projects are created every week. The security team wants to avoid writing and updating a separate IAM policy for every project. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create one identity policy that allows the EC2 actions only when the Project tag on the instance equals the Project tag of the calling principal
- B. Create a customer managed policy for each project that allows EC2 actions when the instance's Project tag equals that project's name, and attach it to the project's group
- C. Create a permission set for each project in IAM Identity Center that allows EC2 actions on the instances that carry that project's tag
- D. Create an AWS Resource Groups group for every project from the Project tag and grant each engineer access to the instances in that group
- E. Tag every instance with a Project tag and pass each engineer's project to the session as an attribute for access control

**Answer:** A, E

**Explanation:** Attribute-based access control compares the Project tag of the resource with the Project tag of the principal in one policy, and Identity Center passes the engineer's project attribute into the session, so a new project needs only correct tags.
- Policy per project: a new policy to write and attach each week (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Permission set per project: the same weekly maintenance in Identity Center (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Resource Groups per project: groups organize resources but do not grant permissions (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/introduction_attribute-based-access-control.html
> 🇻🇳 Nhiều dự án, thêm liên tục → ABAC: một policy so khớp aws:PrincipalTag với thẻ tài nguyên.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-20
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: management
- services: Organizations
- tags: scp, allow-list, multi-account
- difficulty: hard
- time: 165
- skills: 1.1.s4, 1.1.k1
- concept: An SCP allow list works only when FullAWSAccess is replaced at that level; deny lists leave future services open
- refs: 06-management-governance.md
- hint: Đề chặn cả dịch vụ AWS ra mắt sau này — SCP kiểu allow hay deny làm được, và SCP mặc định đang gắn ở OU ảnh hưởng thế nào?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company has 20 sandbox accounts in a Sandbox OU. The sandbox accounts must be able to use only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3 and AWS Lambda, and no other AWS service, including services that AWS launches in the future, even if a sandbox administrator attaches AdministratorAccess to a user. The organization has all features enabled, and the default FullAWSAccess SCP is attached to the root, the Sandbox OU and every account. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Attach the allow-list SCP to each of the 20 sandbox accounts and keep FullAWSAccess attached to the Sandbox OU and to the accounts
- B. Create an SCP that allows only the ec2:*, s3:* and lambda:* actions and attach it to the Sandbox OU for the 20 sandbox accounts
- C. Detach the FullAWSAccess SCP from the organization root so that the allow list is the policy that grants access above the accounts
- D. Create an SCP that denies every other AWS service by name, leaving EC2, S3 and Lambda untouched, and attach it to the Sandbox OU
- E. Detach the FullAWSAccess SCP from the Sandbox OU so that the allow list is the only policy granting access at that level

**Answer:** B, E

**Explanation:** For an allow list, an Allow for the three services must exist at every level, and FullAWSAccess must be removed where the list is applied, or that level still allows everything. As an SCP, it caps even an AdministratorAccess user.
- Allow list on each account with FullAWSAccess kept: FullAWSAccess still allows every service at each level (dùng sai tính năng)
- Detaching FullAWSAccess from the root: removes access for every account in the organization (giải bài toán khác)
- Deny list by service name: services launched later are not denied (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html
> 🇻🇳 Allow-list SCP: gỡ FullAWSAccess ở cấp OU đó và gắn SCP chỉ cho phép dịch vụ cần dùng; deny-list bỏ sót dịch vụ mới.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-21
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: management
- services: Organizations, S3
- tags: rcp, data-perimeter, scp
- difficulty: hard
- time: 135
- skills: 1.1.s4, 1.1.s5, 1.1.k1
- concept: A resource control policy restricts access to resources in member accounts by principals outside the organization, which SCPs cannot do
- refs: 05-security-services.md, 06-management-governance.md
- hint: Cần chặn principal bên ngoài tổ chức truy cập bucket kể cả khi dev tự thêm bucket policy — SCP chỉ kiểm soát principal bên trong.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company stores sensitive datasets in Amazon S3 buckets across 80 member accounts in AWS Organizations. Developers sometimes write bucket policies with overly broad principals. The security team must guarantee that principals outside the organization can never read objects in any bucket of the member accounts, even if a developer later adds a bucket policy that grants an external account access. AWS services that read the buckets on behalf of the organization must keep working, and individual buckets must not need changes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Attach a service control policy to the organization root that denies S3 actions when the request comes from a principal outside the organization's accounts
- B. Attach an SCP to the root that denies s3:PutBucketPolicy to every principal except the security team's role in each member account
- C. Enable IAM Access Analyzer for the organization and run an automatic remediation that removes external principals from bucket policies when a finding appears
- D. Attach a resource control policy to the root that denies S3 actions unless aws:PrincipalOrgID matches, excepting AWS service principals

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** A resource control policy sets the maximum access to resources in member accounts for any caller, including outsiders, so it overrides any bucket policy. The organization ID condition and the service exception keep internal access working.
- SCP on the root: affects principals in the organization's accounts, not external callers (dùng sai tính năng)
- SCP blocking PutBucketPolicy: stops new policies, but existing broad grants still let outsiders read (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Access Analyzer with remediation: acts after access is granted and edits individual bucket policies (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_rcps.html
> 🇻🇳 Chặn principal ngoài tổ chức truy cập tài nguyên → RCP (aws:PrincipalOrgID); SCP chỉ giới hạn principal bên trong.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-22
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: IAM, S3, DynamoDB, Lambda
- tags: resource-based-policies, cross-account-access
- difficulty: medium
- time: 125
- skills: 1.1.s5, 1.1.s3
- concept: A resource-based policy grants cross-account access without the caller giving up its own permissions, unlike assuming a role
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Hàm Lambda phải đọc ở tài khoản A và ghi ở tài khoản B trong cùng một lần chạy — cách nào không bắt đổi danh tính?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

An AWS Lambda function in account B reads objects from an Amazon S3 bucket in account A and writes the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table in account B during the same invocation. The objects must stay in account A, and the developers do not want to add code that switches credentials between the two accounts. The function should keep using its existing execution role. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST code change?

- A. Create an IAM role in account A with read access that trusts the execution role, and have the function assume it through AWS STS before reading the objects
- B. Add a bucket policy in account A that allows the function's execution role in account B to read the objects, and allow the action in the role's policy
- C. Create an IAM role in account A with read access to the bucket and write access to the table, and configure it as the function's execution role
- D. Create a replication rule that copies the objects to a bucket in account B and change the function to read from the replica

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** A bucket policy names the execution role from account B, which keeps its own credentials, and the role's identity policy also allows the read. Cross-account access needs both, and no credential switching is needed.
- Assuming a role in account A: the code must switch credentials between the read and the write (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Role from account A as the execution role: a function's execution role must belong to the function's own account (đặt sai chỗ)
- Replicating to account B: copies the objects out of account A (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-cross-account-resource-access.html
> 🇻🇳 Truy cập chéo tài khoản không đổi danh tính → resource-based policy (bucket policy) + quyền ở identity policy của người gọi.

## Q ai-20261022-a11-23
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: S3, SQS, IAM
- tags: resource-based-policies, confused-deputy
- difficulty: hard
- time: 135
- skills: 1.1.s5
- concept: S3 event notifications to SQS use the queue's resource policy for the S3 service principal, scoped with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount
- refs: 05-security-services.md, 07-application-integration.md
- hint: S3 giao thông báo với tư cách gì — và điều kiện nào ngăn bucket của tài khoản khác dùng hàng đợi (confused deputy)?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company configures Amazon S3 event notifications so that a bucket sends messages to an Amazon SQS queue in the same account. The configuration fails validation because the queue's access policy has no statements. The security team also requires that only this specific bucket can send messages to the queue, and that buckets in other accounts cannot use the queue even if they name it as a destination. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Add a statement to the queue's access policy that allows the s3.amazonaws.com service principal to call sqs:SendMessage, with an aws:PrincipalOrgID condition for the organization
- B. Add a statement to the queue's access policy that allows the bucket owner's account root principal to call sqs:SendMessage on the queue
- C. Add a statement to the queue's access policy that allows the s3.amazonaws.com service principal to call sqs:SendMessage, with aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount conditions
- D. Add a statement to the queue's access policy that allows the s3.amazonaws.com service principal to call sqs:SendMessage, with an aws:SourceAccount condition for the company's account

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** S3 delivers notifications as a service principal, so the queue's resource-based policy must allow it. The aws:SourceArn condition limits delivery to this bucket and aws:SourceAccount to this account, preventing the confused deputy problem.
- aws:PrincipalOrgID condition: a service principal does not belong to the organization, so S3 deliveries are rejected (dùng sai tính năng)
- Account root principal: S3 sends messages as its service principal, not as the bucket owner's account (dùng sai tính năng)
- aws:SourceAccount alone: any other bucket in the account could send to the queue (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/grant-destinations-permissions-to-s3.html
> 🇻🇳 S3 → SQS: queue policy cho principal s3.amazonaws.com + điều kiện aws:SourceArn/SourceAccount để chống confused deputy.

A company keeps a central data lake in an Amazon S3 bucket owned by a data platform account in AWS Organizations. About 150 analytics accounts in the same organization read from the bucket through application roles, and new analytics accounts are created every week. The data must never be readable by principals outside the company. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

- A. Add a bucket policy statement that allows read access to principals of the organization through aws:PrincipalOrgID, and let each account grant access to its own roles
- B. Add a bucket policy statement that lists the ARN of every approved analytics role as a principal, and update the statement whenever a role needs access

## Q ai-20261022-a11-26
- domain: secure
- task: 1.1
- topic: security
- services: IAM, STS
- tags: cross-account-access, external-id, confused-deputy
- difficulty: medium
- time: 125
- skills: 1.1.s3
- concept: A third-party cross-account role should require a vendor-generated external ID to prevent the confused deputy problem
- refs: 05-security-services.md
- hint: Nhà cung cấp phục vụ hàng trăm khách hàng dùng chung tài khoản AWS — giá trị nào trong trust policy ngăn khách khác lợi dụng?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A company hires a SaaS vendor to analyze its AWS costs. The vendor serves hundreds of customers and reaches each customer account by assuming a cross-account IAM role. The security team wants the vendor to be able to assume the company's role only when acting on the company's behalf, so that another customer of the vendor cannot trick the vendor's service into accessing the company's account. The solution must not share long-term credentials. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Create an IAM role that trusts the vendor's AWS account and requires MFA through the aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition in the trust policy
- B. Create an IAM role that trusts the vendor's AWS account and add an aws:SourceIp condition to the trust policy that lists the vendor's published public IP ranges
- C. Create an IAM role whose trust policy names the vendor service's specific IAM role ARN as the principal instead of the vendor's whole account
- D. Create an IAM role that trusts the vendor's AWS account and requires a unique external ID, generated by the vendor for the company, in the sts:ExternalId condition

A shared-services account hosts a latency-sensitive in-memory cache cluster in the Availability Zone named us-east-1a of that account. A development account must run its EC2 instances in the same physical Availability Zone as the cache to avoid inter-AZ latency and data transfer charges. The team launched the instances in us-east-1a of the development account, but the bill still shows inter-AZ data transfer for the cache traffic. - D. Look up the AZ ID of the cache subnet in the shared-services account and launch the instances in the development account's subnet that has the same AZ ID

A company runs six microservices as Amazon ECS tasks on a shared cluster of EC2 container instances. Each microservice needs a different set of Amazon S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables. - B. Run each microservice on its own capacity provider backed by a dedicated Auto Scaling group whose instance profile holds just that service's permissions
- C. Create an IAM role for each microservice, set it as the task execution role in its task definition, and trim the shared permissions from the instance profile
- D. Create an IAM role for each microservice, set it as the task role in its task definition, and trim the shared permissions from the instance profile

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** A task role delivers temporary credentials to the containers of one task definition through the standard SDK credential chain, so each service gets only its own permissions and the instance profile can shrink.

- Dedicated capacity provider per service: works, but adds six Auto Scaling groups to operate (tốn vận hành hơn)
- Task execution role: used by the ECS agent to pull images and send logs, not by the application code (dùng sai tính năng)

- hint: ACL không nhớ trạng thái — gói trả lời của kết nối TCP đi tới cổng đích nào, và rule hiện tại có cho phép cổng đó không?

- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22

A software company hardened two private subnets by replacing their default network ACLs with custom ones. An application server in subnet A calls a licensing service on TCP port 8443 that runs on an instance in subnet B. The security groups on both instances are correct and allow the traffic. Each custom network ACL has allow rules for TCP 8443 in both directions between the two subnet CIDR ranges and no other allow rules. Calls now time out. The team must restore connectivity while keeping the network ACLs as restrictive as possible. Which change will meet these requirements?

- A. Add entries to both network ACLs that allow the full TCP port range in both directions between the two subnet CIDR ranges, next to the 8443 entries
- B. Change the response-path entries so that outbound on subnet B and inbound on subnet A permit the ephemeral TCP range between the two subnet CIDRs
- C. Add entries so that outbound on subnet A and inbound on subnet B permit the ephemeral TCP range between the two subnet CIDRs
- D. Add an inbound rule to the application server's security group that allows the ephemeral TCP range from the subnet B CIDR range

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Network ACLs are stateless, so the reply to a request on port 8443 returns to an ephemeral port on the client. Allowing the ephemeral range only on the reply path (subnet B outbound, subnet A inbound) restores traffic with the narrowest rules.
- Full TCP port range in both directions: works, but opens far more than needed (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Ephemeral range on subnet A outbound and subnet B inbound: that is the request path, so replies stay blocked (đặt sai chỗ)
- Ephemeral range in the security group: security groups are stateful and already allow replies; the ACLs still drop them (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/custom-network-acl.html
> 🇻🇳 NACL là stateless: mở dải cổng ephemeral đúng chiều trả lời (B ra, A vào); security group thì stateful nên không cần.

A publishing company serves premium PDF files from an Amazon S3 bucket through an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses an origin access identity (OAI). A new policy requires every object to be encrypted with SSE-KMS by using a customer managed key, and the bucket must not be reachable directly from the internet. - D. Replace the OAI with an origin access control and allow the CloudFront service principal for this distribution in the bucket policy, keeping the key policy unchanged

A payments company ingests transaction events from its mobile app and processes them with a fleet of worker instances. Events for the same customer account must be processed in the exact order they were sent, but events for different accounts can be processed in parallel. The app sometimes retries a send after a network timeout, and a retried event must not be processed twice. The company expects steady growth and wants to add workers without code changes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Send events to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue, use the account ID as the message group ID, enable content-based deduplication, and run multiple consumers on the queue.

- C. Send events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with the account ID as the partition key, and run one consumer for each shard so that the shards are processed in parallel.
- D. Send events to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue, use the account ID as the message group ID, set a new random deduplication ID on every send attempt, and run multiple consumers.

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** FIFO keeps order within a message group and drops duplicate sends, and the account ID as group ID still allows parallel processing across accounts.

An e-commerce platform is built from microservices. When a customer places an order, the order service calls the payment, inventory, and shipping services one after another over HTTP. When the shipping service slows down, order requests time out and customers see errors even though payment succeeded. The customer must still see the payment result immediately, but inventory reservation and shipping can complete a few seconds later. Teams must be able to deploy their services independently. Which combination of changes will improve resilience? (Choose TWO)

- A. Send the payment request to an Amazon SQS queue as well and email the customer the payment result a few seconds after the order is placed.
- B. Keep the payment call synchronous through an internal load balancer and add client-side timeouts and retries with exponential backoff.
- C. Orchestrate the payment, inventory, and shipping calls in an AWS Step Functions Express workflow that the order service invokes synchronously for each order.
- D. Publish an OrderPlaced event to an Amazon SNS topic and have the inventory and shipping services consume it through their own Amazon SQS queues.
- E. Raise the client timeouts and the retry counts on every service call so that slow dependencies get more time and more attempts to respond.

**Answer:** B, D

**Explanation:** The payment result is needed immediately, so that call stays synchronous with timeouts and backoff; inventory and shipping can finish later, so an SNS topic with a queue per service decouples them and a slow shipping service no longer fails orders.
- Asynchronous payment with an email: the customer must see the payment result immediately (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Synchronous Express workflow: the order still waits for shipping, so a slow shipping service still fails the request (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Longer timeouts and more retries: callers wait longer and the slowdown cascades (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-sqs-as-subscriber.html
> 🇻🇳 Bước cần kết quả ngay giữ đồng bộ (timeout + retry backoff); bước làm sau được thì tách bằng SNS → SQS; gộp dịch vụ hay tăng timeout đều sai hướng.

A photo-printing company runs worker instances in an Auto Scaling group that pull print jobs from an Amazon SQS queue. Job arrival rates change unpredictably during the day, and the average processing time per job is a stable 6 seconds. The company wants jobs to wait no longer than about 2 minutes, without keeping unused instances. The group scales on average CPU utilization, which stays low even when the backlog grows because workers spend most of their time waiting on a slow third-party API. Which scaling approach will meet these requirements?

- A. Use a target tracking policy on the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric of the queue with a backlog target of 20 messages, the number of jobs one instance can process in 2 minutes.
- B. Use a target tracking policy on a backlog-per-instance metric, calculated as queue length divided by in-service instances, with a target based on acceptable latency and job processing time.
- C. Add a predictive scaling policy that forecasts the number of workers from the job arrivals of the previous two weeks and launches the workers before the forecast load arrives.
- D. Lower the CPU target value of the existing target tracking policy so that the group scales out at a lower average CPU utilization of the instances that process a job.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Backlog per instance scales the fleet with the waiting work, using a target of acceptable latency divided by processing time (here 120 s ÷ 6 s = 20 messages per instance), independent of CPU.
- Raw queue length with a fixed target: the metric ignores how many instances share the backlog, so a per-instance figure applied to the whole queue makes the group scale out of proportion (dùng sai tính năng)
- Predictive scaling: forecasts recurring patterns, but job arrivals change unpredictably (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Lower CPU target: CPU stays low while workers wait on the API, so it is the wrong signal (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html

A target tracking policy on the queue backlog scales the group in when the backlog shrinks, and the group terminates instances that are in the middle of an export, which corrupts customers' output files. - refs: E-kien-truc-database.md, F-so-sanh-database-theo-dac-diem.md
- hint: Giá đổi hiếm nhưng khách vẫn thấy giá cũ tới hết TTL — chiến lược nào cập nhật cache cùng lúc với lần ghi vào CSDL?

- created: 2026-10-22

An e-commerce company caches product prices in Amazon ElastiCache to reduce read load on its Amazon Aurora database. The application uses lazy loading with a 15-minute TTL. When merchants change a price, shoppers keep seeing the old price for up to 15 minutes, which violates a pricing-accuracy policy. Price changes are infrequent and reads are heavy, and the team wants to keep the cache hit rate high without increasing read traffic on the database. Which change will meet these requirements?

- A. Reduce the TTL on every cached price to 30 seconds so that shoppers see a changed price within half a minute while most reads still hit the cache.
- B. Capture price changes with Aurora Database Activity Streams and have a Lambda function update the cached price for each change that the stream reports.
- C. Update the application so that each price write to Aurora also writes the new price to the cache (write-through), and keep the TTL as a safety net.
- D. Migrate the cache to Amazon ElastiCache Serverless so that it scales automatically with the read load and keeps serving prices from memory.

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** Write-through updates the cache whenever the database is written, so prices are not stale, and the TTL keeps rarely read entries from piling up.
- 30-second TTL: shoppers still see old prices for up to half a minute, which the policy forbids (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Database Activity Streams: an encrypted audit feed for monitoring database activity, not a change feed for updating a cache (dùng sai tính năng)
- ElastiCache Serverless: scales capacity, but lazily loaded entries stay stale until their TTL ends (giải bài toán khác)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Strategies.html
> 🇻🇳 Cache-aside (lazy loading) gây dữ liệu cũ tới hết TTL → thêm write-through (ghi DB thì ghi cache) + giữ TTL; TTL ngắn vẫn còn giá cũ, Database Activity Streams là luồng audit.

- D. Remove one read replica, turn on Multi-AZ for the remaining read replica, and send the dashboard queries to that highly available replica

- D. Turn on capacity rebalancing for the Auto Scaling group in us-west-2 so that failed launches are retried in other Availability Zones
- E. Create On-Demand Capacity Reservations in us-west-2 for the instances and Availability Zones that a disaster recovery will need

**Answer:** C, E

**Explanation:** VcpuLimitExceeded means the DR Region's On-Demand quota is too low (quotas apply per Region), and InsufficientInstanceCapacity means capacity was not available, which On-Demand Capacity Reservations secure in advance, so both fixes are needed before a disaster.
- Regional Reserved Instances: give a billing discount but reserve no capacity (dùng sai tính năng).
- Quota increase in us-east-1: quotas apply per Region, and the failures happened in us-west-2 (đặt sai chỗ).
- Capacity rebalancing: replaces Spot Instances at elevated risk of interruption, not failed On-Demand launches (dùng sai tính năng).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-reservations.html

- B. Create failover alias records with us-east-1 as the primary Region and eu-west-1 as the secondary Region, with Evaluate Target Health turned on

A company runs a Windows file server on a single EC2 instance in one Availability Zone, with an EBS volume that serves SMB shares to 300 users and applications joined to Active Directory. An Availability Zone outage made the shares unavailable for hours. The company wants a managed solution that keeps the shares available through an Availability Zone failure with automatic failover, preserves NTFS permissions and Active Directory integration, and needs no client changes, with the LEAST operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements?

- A. Move the data to Amazon S3 and serve it through an Amazon S3 File Gateway SMB file share that is joined to Active Directory
- B. Create a second Windows file server instance joined to Active Directory in another Availability Zone and replicate the shares with DFS Replication, using scripts to manage failover
- C. Migrate the data to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system joined to Active Directory
- D. Migrate the data to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Single-AZ file system joined to Active Directory and enable daily backups

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ runs an active and a standby file server in two Availability Zones with synchronous replication and automatic failover, keeping the same DNS name, NTFS permissions, and Active Directory integration for clients.
- S3 File Gateway: the gateway appliance runs on a single VM or instance, so an Availability Zone failure still takes the shares offline (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- A second self-managed server with DFS Replication: adds patching and failover scripting (tốn vận hành hơn).
- FSx Single-AZ with daily backups: an Availability Zone outage still takes the shares offline until a restore (vi phạm ràng buộc).

An online ticketing site runs a PHP application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The web tier is stateless: shopping carts and sign-in sessions are stored in an Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) cluster that has a single node in one Availability Zone. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

- B. Enable daily automatic backups on the existing single-node cluster and restore the newest backup to a new node whenever the current node fails
- C. Turn on cluster mode and split the session keys across three shards without replicas so that a node failure affects a single shard

A company's image-processing service receives bursts of requests from a mobile app. The service calls an Amazon DynamoDB table and a rate-limited partner API. During bursts it receives ProvisionedThroughputExceededException from DynamoDB and HTTP 429 from the partner, retries immediately in a tight loop, then crashes, and requests are lost. The company wants the service to degrade gracefully and recover without losing requests. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose THREE)

- B. Retry throttled calls with exponential backoff and jitter instead of retrying immediately

- F. Switch the DynamoDB table to on-demand capacity mode so that throughput follows the traffic

A logistics company runs a self-managed PostgreSQL database on a large Nitro-based Amazon EC2 instance. The 3 TiB data volume is a General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume, and month-end batch jobs now saturate it at about 9,000 IOPS and 250 MiB/s. Monitoring shows that the database needs a sustained 45,000 IOPS and 1,200 MiB/s. Single-digit millisecond latency is acceptable, the database cannot be stopped, and the company wants the lowest-cost fix. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

A media company's web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. When a user uploads a video, the web server transcodes it synchronously, which takes up to 20 minutes of CPU time. During promotions the web tier saturates, page requests time out, and uploads are lost when instances are replaced. The company wants the web tier and the transcoding workers to scale independently, to absorb bursts without losing uploads, and to add worker capacity in proportion to the amount of waiting work. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Store each upload in Amazon S3 and configure an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function to transcode each video.
- B. Store each upload in Amazon S3, send a message that references it to an Amazon SQS queue, and run the transcoding workers in a separate Auto Scaling group.
- C. Configure target tracking on the queue's ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric so that the worker Auto Scaling group's capacity follows the number of waiting messages.
- D. Configure target tracking on a backlog-per-instance metric calculated from the queue length and the number of in-service instances.
- E. Configure step scaling on the worker group's average CPU utilization so that workers are added whenever busy workers exceed 70 percent.

**Answer:** B, D

**Explanation:** The queue buffers uploads so the two tiers scale independently and nothing is lost, and a backlog-per-instance metric (queue length divided by in-service instances) gives target tracking a value that moves in proportion to the waiting work.
- S3 event invoking Lambda: decouples, but a function run is limited to 15 minutes, shorter than the 20-minute jobs (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Target tracking on raw queue length: it does not change in proportion to group size, so it cannot converge (dùng sai tính năng)
- Step scaling on worker CPU: busy workers run near full CPU whatever the backlog, so capacity does not follow waiting work (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html

A fintech company hosts a customer-facing REST API on AWS Lambda behind Amazon API Gateway. The functions use the Java 17 runtime and load a large dependency framework during start-up, so the first request that reaches each new execution environment takes several seconds. Traffic is spiky: it jumps from a handful of requests to thousands per second within a minute after each push notification, and the marketing team sends the notifications at fixed, published times. The company wants to remove this start-up delay without rewriting the functions. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Raise the memory setting of each function to the maximum value so that the start-up code finishes faster on every new execution environment.
- B. Enable Lambda SnapStart on each function, publish a version, and send traffic to that version through an alias.
- C. Set reserved concurrency on each function to the expected peak so that Lambda keeps initialized execution environments ready for traffic.
- D. Configure provisioned concurrency on a published version and adjust it with Application Auto Scaling to match the expected traffic.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** For Java runtimes SnapStart adds no extra charge and resumes new execution environments from a cached snapshot of the initialized function, which removes most of the start-up delay.

- Reserved concurrency: only guarantees and caps how many environments can run; it pre-initializes none (dùng sai tính năng)
- Provisioned concurrency: keeps initialized environments ready, but you pay for them all the time (tốn chi phí hơn)

An engineering firm runs tightly coupled computational fluid dynamics simulations that use the Message Passing Interface (MPI) across 64 Amazon EC2 instances. A payments company writes transaction events to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Five independent applications, including a fraud-scoring service, read every record by using the shared-throughput GetRecords API. After the fifth application was added, the fraud service receives records about a second after they are written, and several consumers report read throttling. The fraud service needs the lowest possible propagation delay, and every consumer must still receive each record. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Register each consumer application as an enhanced fan-out consumer so that each one receives dedicated read throughput per shard
- B. Increase the number of shards with UpdateShardCount so that each consumer application receives more total read throughput
- C. Move each consumer application to an AWS Lambda event source mapping with a batching window of zero seconds on the stream
- D. Reduce the polling interval of each consumer so that the applications call GetRecords more often and read records sooner from the shards

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** Shared-throughput consumers split 2 MB per second per shard, which raises delay as consumers are added. Enhanced fan-out gives each registered consumer its own pipe per shard and pushes records over HTTP/2, so the propagation delay stays low.
- More shards: adds total throughput, but every consumer still polls and shares each shard's read limits, so delay stays above push delivery (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Lambda event source mappings without enhanced fan-out: still read through shared-throughput GetRecords polling (dùng sai tính năng)
- More frequent polling: consumers share the same per-shard limits, so throttling increases (dùng sai tính năng)

A logistics company streams GPS events from 60,000 trucks into a provisioned-mode Kinesis data stream. Producers use the truck's depot ID as the partition key, and about 25 depots exist. One central depot generates more traffic than a single shard can ingest, so producers receive WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded errors while most other shards are nearly idle. Events from the same truck must be processed in order. The company must stop the throttling. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Split the busy shard with the SplitShard API so that the central depot's records are divided between two new child shards
- B. Change the partition key from the depot ID to the truck ID so that the records of the busy depot spread across the shards
- C. Switch the stream to on-demand capacity mode so that Kinesis Data Streams adds shard capacity automatically as traffic grows
- D. Use the truck ID plus a random suffix as the partition key so that each truck's records spread evenly across several shards

An analytics company runs a nightly log-processing job on a Linux Amazon EC2 instance. The job streams through about 8 TiB of sequential log files on a data volume and needs sustained throughput of about 300 MiB/s. Other batch jobs read the same files throughout the day, so the data is not cold. Random I/O is minimal and the volume is not the boot volume. The team wants to minimize storage cost. - D. Create a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volume of about 10 TiB and provision enough IOPS to sustain the required throughput.

A media company serves a marketing site and a product-image catalog through Amazon CloudFront, about 400 million requests a day. For every viewer request the company must rewrite legacy URL paths to new paths and normalize the query string to improve the cache hit ratio, and every response must carry security headers. - B. Use a mixed instances policy with an On-Demand base sized for the campaign peak, Spot above it, several instance types, and price-capacity-optimized allocation

- D. Use a mixed instances policy with a small On-Demand base, Spot above it, the current single instance type, lowest-price allocation and Capacity Rebalancing

The team will put an Amazon ElastiCache cache in front of the database to reduce database load. Memory cost matters: the cache should not hold items that nobody reads, and the application can tolerate data that is a few minutes old. Which caching strategy will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Use lazy loading that fills the cache on a read miss, and keep each cached item with no expiration time.
- B. Use lazy loading that fills the cache on a read miss, and give every cached item a time to live of a few minutes.

- D. Use write-behind caching so that updates go to the cache first and are flushed to the database asynchronously a few minutes later.

A telemetry service stores device records in an Amazon DynamoDB table that uses provisioned capacity mode. Each record is 6 KB. At peak, the application performs 500 reads per second, which can use eventually consistent reads, and 120 writes per second. The team wants to provision just enough capacity to avoid throttling at peak, at the lowest cost. Which provisioned throughput settings will meet these requirements?

- A. Set the table's provisioned throughput to 500 read capacity units and 720 write capacity units.
- B. Set the table's provisioned throughput to 1,000 read capacity units and 720 write capacity units.
- C. Set the table's provisioned throughput to 250 read capacity units and 120 write capacity units.
- D. Set the table's provisioned throughput to 375 read capacity units and 720 write capacity units.

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** A 6 KB item rounds up to 8 KB (two 4 KB units) and an eventually consistent read costs half, so each read needs 1 RCU (500 total); each 6 KB write needs 6 WCUs (720 total).
- 1,000 RCUs: assumes strongly consistent reads, though eventual is allowed (tốn chi phí hơn)
- 250 RCUs and 120 WCUs: ignores item size, so peak traffic would be throttled (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- 375 RCUs: does not round the item size up to 4 KB multiples, so reads throttle (vi phạm ràng buộc)
